A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAGEA framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Meta-World MT10 success rates, learning curves, component ablations and trajectory examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Fetch evaluations, alternative VLM/text-encoder experiments and convergence-time measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same structured feedback, keyframe weighting, alignment losses, delta rewards and adaptive failure-gated SAC training. The default Qwen2.5-VL-3B/GPT-2 pipeline remains unchanged; alternative models are evaluated as experimental variants.

E1.justification: v2 adds four Gymnasium-Robotics Fetch tasks: Reach, Push, Slide and Pick-and-Place. This extends evaluation beyond Sawyer-based Meta-World to another robot/environment and includes sliding requirements. Both existing MT10 goal settings remain.

E2.justification: Appendix C.1 adds comparison variants using SmolVLM2, InternVL2 and OpenQwen2VL, and LIV, BGE and MPNet text encoders. Existing MT10 baseline membership is unchanged; the Fetch comparison reuses SAC, Relay and FuRL.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 50-step sparse-reward Fetch protocol, alternative backbone/encoder configurations and wall-clock time to convergence as an evaluation measure. The stated 500-step MT10 setup remains. Removed hyperparameter documentation does not establish changes to existing training settings.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds substantive tests of dependence on VLM and text-encoder choices across five observable MT10 tasks, plus computational-efficiency analysis across nine task/settings. Existing component ablations and qualitative cases are retained, including the results moved from v1 Table 7 to v2 Table 10.

E5.justification: Five-seed MT10 reporting and three-seed ablation summaries remain, and new tables extend the existing mean/standard-deviation practice. Removing v1 Table 5 and Section 6 also removes the explicit random-seed 0 entry and seed-fixing declaration. This is lost seed documentation, not evidence of fewer runs.

E6.justification: Existing MT10 and component-ablation results remain unchanged. New Fetch Table 3 reports average success of 51.67% for LAGEA versus 44.17% for FuRL. Appendix C adds backbone/encoder results and convergence times averaging 92.36 versus 94.90 minutes, with LAGEA slower in some settings.

T1.justification: The keyframe definitions, alignment objectives, reward potentials and adaptive shaping equations are mathematically unchanged. Equations are reformatted, and neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion extend the performance claims to Fetch while retaining the central language-feedback contribution. The new 17% Fetch advantage is approximately relative: Table 3 shows a 7.50-percentage-point difference, although Section 4.1.2 incorrectly calls it absolute.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets model-choice experiments as evidence of robustness and argues that fewer environment steps compensate for VLM inference overhead. The existing hallucination, real-robot generalization and long-horizon limitations are retained in Appendix M.

D1.justification: v2 removes the comprehensive hyperparameter table in v1 Appendix A.8, including learning rate, batch size, training budget, evaluation frequency and shaping settings. It also removes Section 6's repository and rerun disclosures. Hardware and most software details remain, while Fetch instructions/API details and timing information are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting Fetch and the alternative models/encoders, including Plappert et al., InternVL, SmolVLM, OpenQwen2VL, M3/BGE and MPNet. The main and extended related-work discussions retain substantially the same positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v2 reorders the ablation subsections, reframes RQ3 around robustness, restructures the appendices and moves limitations to Appendix M. It also makes localized abstract/conclusion and author/header edits and adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two columns, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. v1 Figures 4 and 5 become v2 Figure 4(a,b). v2 adds Fetch and appendix-result displays, expands the instruction table and removes the hyperparameter table.

improvement.justification: Fetch evaluation and the new model-choice/runtime studies broaden empirical support and address useful questions about robustness and computational cost. However, v2 removes substantial reproduction information and misstates the Fetch gain as absolute. These material gains in validation and losses in reproducibility and reporting accuracy prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
